steps: docs: review.md Which widths, merge doc, skill paragraph on card

assign.now: widthsFor(files, numstat, pages) exported from review.mjs, with splitPatch() and writeNoReviewPass() as shared helpers; review.mjs's own page-shots step and a new --widths flag now use it instead of the fixed four

decision.question: how to detect a 'layout word' without a diff-content param in widthsFor's signature
options: read file content from disk inside widthsFor (needs a root dir, wrong tree when run from the main repo)
attach an optional .patch field (that file's own diff text) to each files[] entry, built by the caller via a new exported splitPatch()
decision.why: keeps widthsFor pure and unit-testable with no fs/git calls, and the real caller (review.mjs's main(), and merge.mjs's --quick path) already has the full diff text in hand

decision.question: max-width contains the word width, which collided with the layout-word regex (rule 2 always beat rule 3)
options: exclude the width inside max-width/min-width from the layout-word regex with a negative lookbehind
decision.why: keeps the owner's own stated rule order (1,2,3,4) intact; caught by the widthsFor unit test before it ever reached merge.mjs

decision.question: where does --quick's shot + no-agent review record live when there's no dated task dir (the common case for a voice quick-fix)
options: write nothing without a task dir
a shared public/framework/ai/quick-fix/ task dir used by every quick fix (append-only task.jsonl, review.md overwritten each time but unread)
guess a dated task dir from the branch name the same way reviewGate already does, falling back to public/framework/ai/quick-fix/
decision.chose: the fallback, via a shared guessTaskDir() helper reused by both reviewGate and --quick
decision.why: matches the brief's own literal fallback path (public/framework/ai/quick-fix/shots/<sha>/) and removes the duplicate branch-name-guessing logic that used to live only inside reviewGate

decision.question: review size
decision.why: self-evident: Server/ code only (merge.mjs, review.mjs, review.test.mjs, two docs), no new page or module; review.test.mjs is a plain unit test beside the module it tests

running node Server/review.mjs public/framework/ai/2026-10-01/quick-fix-path/quick-merge --size light --why '...' in the background (bts63xjc7) — Server-only change, no page, per the brief's own review instruction

findings.text: Could not find, in this diff, the drafted paragraph for the `review` skill ("pick widths by what changed") that point 3 of requirements.md asks to be put on the card for the Servex mastermind — it may have gone out via a card tool outside the file diff; worth confirming on card `2026/10/01/the-fast-path-fix-this-by-voice-is-live` before closing that deliverable.

`Server/README.md:21` adds `--quick` as one long run-in sentence inside the existing merge paragraph rather than the "three lines" requirements.md point 3 asked for; reads fine, just denser than asked.

`Server/merge.mjs:462` (`const width = widths[0]`) only ever takes the FIRST width `widthsFor` returns for `--quick`'s own screenshot, even on the rare quick-eligible change where `widthsFor` returns more than one width (e.g. a 1-line `flex`/`grid` edit matches rule 2 and would want all four). This matches the JSON contract's singular `width` field from requirements.md point 2, so it's not a spec violation, but it does mean a layout-word quick-fix only gets evidence at 400, never at wider widths — worth knowing if that case shows up in practice.

requirements.md's "Proof" line 2 asks to show `--quick`'s "one shot" together with the JSON+`ms` on the same scratch run; `quick-proof.mjs` only shows that combination with `shot:null` (because `--skip-smoke` also disables the screenshot step, by design per its own header comment) — the real pixel is proven separately in `shot-proof.mjs` by calling `widthsFor` + `layout-check.mjs` directly, not through `merge.mjs --quick` itself. Reasonable workaround for a scratch repo with no live server, but the literal "one shot through --quick" case is never exercised end-to-end.

Verified independently: `node Server/review.test.mjs` passes all 13 checks, and re-running `proof/quick-proof.mjs` against a fresh scratch dir reproduces both cases (exit 0 + JSON line for the 3-line change, exit 2 + refusal for the 40-line change) exactly as `quick-proof.txt` records. No simpler implementation suggested — `widthsFor` stays under the ~30-line budget with plain `if`s as asked, and the `writeNoReviewPass`/`guessTaskDir`/`splitPatch` extractions remove duplication rather than add it.

answer.reply: noted: confirmed — posted via card_reply to card 2026/10/01/the-fast-path-fix-this-by-voice-is-live before this review ran (the draft paragraph, plus context on which SKILL.md lines it replaces); card tools aren't part of the file diff so the reviewer couldn't see it there.
fixed: Server/README.md now gives --quick its own short paragraph (3 lines) instead of one long sentence appended to the existing merge paragraph.

fixed: Server/merge.mjs's --quick screenshot step now passes layout-check.mjs every width widthsFor returned (widths.join(",")), not just the first, so a layout-word quick change gets real evidence at all four widths; only the final JSON line's own `width` field stays singular, per requirements.md point 2's own schema.

declined: a true one-shot-through-quick proof needs a disposable worktree with a real page edit and a real server, run without --skip-smoke — which means a REAL git merge into michael/dev for a throwaway test branch. Not worth that risk for a proof. shot-proof.mjs instead calls the exact same widthsFor -> layout-check.mjs pair merge.mjs's own screenshot block calls, against a real page, and proves one real png comes out; quick-proof.mjs proves the gate, the merge, and the JSON line on scratch repos. Together they cover the mechanism without ever risking landing a throwaway branch for real.
